summary: Deep-dive the CLOSED_NON_SHIP multi-spine (multi-span) route: (1) was its "spine-0 contamination" lossy-ness actually the SAME bugs we just fixed (cc008587: stale slot-keyed buffers / remap race / global RNG) => fixable?; (2) on-paper bandwidth-bound speed: multi-spine state-copies vs no-copy tree (current 5.14x, replay route 0.86x) on GB10-class chips; (3) drafter-agnostic lens: target is fast+lossless TREE VERIFY for ANY drafter (some models have NO MTP head) - does multi-spine subsume into the general tree verifier or compete? CPU read-only.

synthesis.era_mechanism_and_evidence: MECHANISM (read from era code surviving in HEAD/branches): multi-spine = hidden co-resident REAL vLLM Request clones (ids <req_id>::lumo_ir_sN) created in a monkeypatched Scheduler.add_request (scripts/swe_x86_helpers/relaunch_qwen36_round.py:303-535, commit 1dcc3e5e), each spine a genuine sequence with its OWN native per-request GDN state row and block-table row, co-scheduled in one forward (launcher set max_num_seqs = B x spines). Drafting: spine-0 = native MTP top-1 (== E5 by construction); spine-s = rank-s root token then the ordinary linear MTP chain (:539-601). Per EVENT, the winner's post-accept state row was device-copied to all S-1 siblings via vLLM's own mamba_utils.do_mamba_copy_block across all 48 GDN layers x BOTH conv+ssm tensors (:769-821, 65fb6439) — unconditionally, in both modes. Two committer eras: Era-1 (lossy) published the best-of-spines longest-accepted-prefix winner; Era-2 (the 'lossless' retrofit, 3e6a93ab/e27a6f96) hard-forces spine-0 commit (selector raises on anything else) and fail-closes spines>1 at launch. WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SHOWED: (1) +6.85% (47.50 vs 44.45 tok/s, accept 3.442 vs 2.772) was the Era-1 LOSSY winner-commit route, greedy low-batch 16-prompt fixture; at production B=4 SWE-16 the same route was a speed LOSS (0.74-0.79x, 4/16 vs 8/16 resolved). superset_violations=0 over 19,307 events was a COUNT-only invariant (winner-accept >= spine-0-accept), not output-equality (968e6bde correction). (2) The decisive lossy-ness artifact (Gate B, fr9-spine2-lossless-winner-closeout-20260602): with BI+FLASH_ATTN, same-arm b1-vs-b4 exact in BOTH arms, selector off, copies clean — yet s1-vs-s2 greedy tokens flipped on 2/4 prompts (first_diff_index 18 and 2). Critically, the two arms were SEPARATE BOOTS with DIFFERENT max_num_seqs (4 vs 8) — an uncontrolled boot-config confound. (3) Era-2 selector-off quick-verify: accept/event s2 3.2364 vs s1 3.2628/3.3355 (lowest of three), TV 0.0097 within / 0.0283 beyond a self-floor (0.0188) estimated from ONE run-pair, 4 tasks, 1 run/arm — self-admitted underpowered, 'borderline not clean'. WHAT WAS ATTRIBUTED: 'co-scheduling a hidden spine contaminates spine-0' — a mechanism-level INFERENCE assembled from elimination (attention/GEMM side controlled), vLLM issue #42960 (GDN excluded from batch-invariant mode), and a pattern-match to FR7's packed-tree shared-recurrent-state ceiling (a DIFFERENT mechanism: one unmasked shared scan within a packed tree, since engineered out in FR13 via h_cache+strict_mask). No per-layer/per-op localization was ever done on the spine arm (CUPTI returned 0 rows, the isolated-forward probe crashed); the top-down ladder methodology only arrived in FR12/FR13.
synthesis.reattribution_verdict: DISTINCT-MECHANISM for the route the no-go was actually measured on — the re-attribution hypothesis is REFUTED. The three cc008587 bug classes ((1) committer global-RNG cross-request mixing, (2) stale SLOT-keyed accepted-path/lens buffers, (3) in-place shift-left remap race) live in the FR10/FR13 tree stack (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py / fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py), code that DID NOT EXIST in the multi-spine era. Class-by-class on the FR9 independent-rows arm that produced the binding evidence: REQKEY absent (req-id-keyed mamba_state_idx, groups rebuilt per step from live input_batch — the stock vLLM mechanism; an earlier tensor-row-parity bug of exactly this class WAS found and fixed in-era before the no-go evidence); REMAP race absent (winner copies are batched memcpys between distinct physical blocks, self-copy skipped; the racy shift-left remap is an FR10-rewrite regression); RNG absent (selector OFF, and the decisive Gate B probe was GREEDY — no RNG in play); conv prior-window class absent (native conv path in IR mode). Structurally, the IR winner machinery only WRITES hidden rows — it cannot contaminate spine-0's public stream by construction. Only the FR7/F_a packed-tree route had a genuine REQKEY-class hazard (module-global batch-ordered _LUMO_FA_LAST_ACCEPTED_TREE_ROWS with silent linear fallback), but FR7's collapse (1.66 vs 3.150) was dominated by the architectural unmasked-shared-scan mechanism. The named distinct mechanism: GDN/recurrent-stack BATCH-COMPOSITION (+ boot-config) NON-INVARIANCE — the vLLM #42960 class — and the post-cc008587 re-probe proves it is STILL LIVE (greedy B=4 0/4 residual explicitly 'outside the 3 channels'; B=1 bit-exact). So cc008587 gives no new reason to expect a different multi-spine outcome. CAVEAT in the user's own FR11 sense: the no-go's EVIDENCE is weak (e2e-only, never localized, 1-pair noise floor, a bit-exact-greedy bar that NATIVE ITSELF fails — FR13 measured native-vs-native only 4/8 exact, and the pos18 'lossy' example was a native artifact), so under the current within-floor bar multi-spine was never decisively failed (TV 0.0097 within floor vs s1b) — OVERTURNABLE-pending-retest in the narrow evidentiary sense, but NOT via cc008587, and the user's CLOSED_NON_SHIP binding (968e6bde) additionally rests on non-statistical grounds (copy cost doesn't scale; count-only superset) that no bug fix touches.
synthesis.speed_verdict: SLOWER on paper than the replay-route tree at EVERY S, with no crossover, on any weight-bandwidth-bound chip; faster only than the current (bug-state) tree. Accounting at B=4 MTP-5 (ssm row 3.146MB x 48 GDN layers x B=4 = 0.604 GB per row-touch; weights 27GB @ 273GB/s = 98.9ms floor): native E5 = 7 rows/layer/req (1R+6W) = 4.23GB -> 114.4ms. Multi-spine = 7S verify + 2(S-1) winner-copy rows (era code copies the winner row to all siblings, conv+ssm, every event): S=2 -> 16 rows = 9.66GB = 1.174x native time/event; S=3 -> 25 rows = 1.348x; S=4 -> 34 rows = 1.522x. Current tree = 36 rows = 21.74GB = 1.561x. Replay-route tree = 6 rows = 3.62GB = 0.981x native. TPS = (accept+1)/time: the shipped LOSSLESS (selector-off) multi-spine commits spine-0 always -> ZERO accept gain (measured 3.2364 vs 3.26-3.34) -> 0.85x/0.74x/0.66x native at S=2/3/4 — pure tax, slower than everything including native. The LOSSY best-of-spines S=2 (the +6.85% route): tokens/event ratio 1.178 almost exactly cancels the 1.174x tax -> ~1.00x native on paper at B=4 — consistent with the measured low-batch +6.85% (model predicts +5-12% where weights dominate) and the measured B=4 production LOSS (0.74-0.79x with overheads). Vs replay tree: the SECOND spine's verify alone (4.23GB) exceeds the ENTIRE replay-tree state budget (3.62GB); break-even needs +19.7%/+37.5%/+55.2% accept over the tree at S=2/3/4 — structurally unreachable because an equal-token-budget tree CONTAINS the S chains (accept >= best-of-S by the superset principle) while replay state cost (2+a rows) is invariant to candidate count (~16.2KiB activations/node vs 3.146MB state row, ~190x). Multi-spine additionally pays (S-1) extra full per-sequence KV reads on the 16 full-attn layers (prefix caching dedupes storage, NOT read bandwidth), growing with context — excluded from the table, so the table is multi-spine's BEST case. Vs the CURRENT contaminated tree multi-spine S=2-4 is on-paper faster (bytes crossover S*=4.22; ~1.8-2.1x TPS at S=2), but that only re-measures the 36-row publish-tax bug state FR13 Half-1/Half-2 is already eliminating. GENERALIZATION: time ∝ W + state + KV; multi-spine marginal = (S-1)[(T+3)·r·Lg·B + K], strictly positive and linear in S; tree-replay marginal vs native <= 0. As W dominates (tiny B, short context) multi-spine approaches parity FROM BELOW, never crossing; as state/KV share grows (bigger B, long contexts, more recurrent layers, weight-resident/MoE chips) the tree's advantage GROWS. The ranking never flips on any current bandwidth-bound chip. Caveats: T=6 for native inferred from num_spec=5; replay 0.86x is counted-touches pending the codegen byte A/B; lossy-S=2 ~1.00x at B=4 is a model extrapolation. None move the no-crossover verdict.
synthesis.drafter_agnostic_verdict: YES — the general tree verifier strictly subsumes multi-spine. S spines = K independent chains sharing only the root = a degenerate tree, expressible directly in the standard candidate-tree descriptor ({node_id, parent_id, depth, sibling_index, token_id, q} per project_fr10_drafter_verifier_interface) with no new mechanism; tree verification is lossless for ANY q (Traversal Verification Thm 3.3), so the subsumption is semantic AND it dominates physically: one forward over one shared KV (ancestry mask = in-register additive bias, ~free per the FR13 FA2-fork analysis), state cost invariant to topology (2+a rows on the replay route) versus multi-spine's linear-in-S state rows + (S-1) duplicated full KV reads + per-event full-state copies — and equal-token-budget tree accept >= best-of-S chains by construction (the tree contains them). REGIME WHERE MULTI-SPINE WINS: none on bandwidth-bound hardware. The hypothesized 'very long independent chains where tree ancestry masks cost more' regime does not exist — the mask is an in-register add inside one attention call, while multi-spine's chains each re-read the full per-sequence KV (S x the KV bandwidth on full-attn layers, growing with context), so long chains make multi-spine WORSE, not better. The only legitimate multi-spine regime is non-performance: an engine that cannot host a tree verifier at all (the vLLM-0.19 capture wall that motivated FR9) — an engineering workaround, never a bandwidth winner. FOR NON-MTP DRAFTERS the right deliverable is exactly the drafter-agnostic tree verifier/committer consuming the descriptor: suffix decoding emits trees natively (forcing it through K chains would discard its shared-prefix structure and multiply state/KV cost), ngram/lookahead drafters emit chains = trivial descriptor instances (a chain is a 1-spine tree; K-chains a degenerate one), Eagle-class heads emit trees by design, and models shipping NO MTP head plug in without touching verify/commit since the verifier knows nothing about how the tree was drafted and losslessness holds for any q. Multi-spine as a separate mechanism would be a strictly weaker, more expensive special case of what the verifier already does.
synthesis.recommendation: DO NOT pursue a multi-spine retest as a route; CONFIRM tree-verifier dominance and keep multi-spine as a topology special-case. Rationale stacked: (1) the cc008587 re-attribution fails — the era no-go ran a different mechanism (GDN batch-composition non-invariance, #42960 class) that is still live post-fix, so the bugs we fixed predict no different outcome; (2) even a PASSED powered retest buys nothing — the lossless (selector-off) variant is 0.85x native on paper with zero accept upside by construction, and the lossy variant is both user-banned (CLOSED_NON_SHIP, 968e6bde — reopening requires explicit user authorization) and only ~1.00x native at B=4, below the replay-route tree's 0.98-1.11x; (3) no crossover exists at any S on any bandwidth-bound chip, and the gap widens exactly where speed matters (bigger B, long SWE contexts). The era's one real residual question (were the Gate B greedy flips boot-config drift vs runtime co-residency?) is settleable by a ~2-3 GPU-hour NATIVE-only max_num_seqs 4-vs-8 cross-boot control — worth running only as cheap evidentiary hygiene if the #42960 noise floor matters for FR13's own B=4 gates (it does, since the same residual gates our e2e bar), NOT as a multi-spine reopening; the ~1.5-2 GPU-day powered within-floor multi-spine retest is NOT recommended at any point — it answers a question whose best-case answer is a slower route. Concrete deliverable actions: (a) continue FR13 Half-2 replay-route as primary (WY fallback) per FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md; (b) formalize the drafter-agnostic candidate-tree descriptor contract (the lightweight refactor already specified in project_fr10_drafter_verifier_interface) so suffix/ngram/Eagle-class drafters plug in without verifier changes; (c) add a cheap K-chain (degenerate-tree, root-fanout-S, no internal branching) descriptor case to the verifier's CPU/oracle gate suite — this captures 100% of multi-spine's semantic value at zero mechanism cost and permanently documents the subsumption; (d) update reference_multispine_not_lossless_closed_nonship-adjacent docs with the new affirmative speed argument (second spine's verify bytes > entire replay-tree budget) so the closure no longer rests solely on the weak-evidence lossy-ness claim.

overreaches: SYN reattribution: 'the IR winner machinery only WRITES hidden rows — it cannot contaminate spine-0's public stream by construction' is true only for the Era-2/selector-off arm that produced the binding evidence (HEAD relaunch_qwen36_round.py:746 commit_idx=primary; :871 token copy is then a self-copy of identical data). Era-1 (65fb6439 :593-599) DID copy a hidden winner row into spine-0's public stream — the claim needs the Era-2 qualifier or it misdescribes the +6.85%/19,307-event route.

SYN drafter_agnostic/speed: 'equal-token-budget tree accept >= best-of-S by the superset principle (the tree contains them)' is exact EQUALITY at greedy (FR13_DECISIVE_TEST.md:4 longest-LCP = unique verify-argmax chain) and theorem-backed only for lossless-vs-lossless (MSS monotone in candidate set); it is NOT a theorem against the era's BIASED lossy best-of-spines committer at temp>0. The defensible argument is empirical: the era's own temp-0.6 lossy edge was ~0.27 recovered tokens/event (recovered_token_total=5271 / 19,307 events) ≈ +6-8% tokens/event, far below the +19.7% S=2 break-even — so the no-crossover verdict survives, but 'by construction' must be replaced by the greedy-equality + measured-bound argument.

SYN recommendation (a): 'continue FR13 Half-2 replay-route as primary' misstates the critical path. The repo's own docs make the ACCEPTANCE-DEFICIT ladder (Half-1) the gating work: FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md:50 (1.432x more forwards = accept gap 'fixed by Half 1'), :75 ('Lossless and faster are ONE outcome'), FR13_COMMITTER_TOPOLOGY_REDTEAM.md:116-152 ('There is no committer or topology change to make. The single open bug is verify-forward drift' = the open Gate-A grind, accept 1.199 -> 3.076), and HEAD commit 2c4da209 ('FR13 accept ladder'). The 2-3 GPU-hour native-only max_num_seqs control is justified ONLY as input to the ladder's e2e noise-floor bar and must not preempt ladder GPU time; descriptor/K-chain/doc items (b)-(d) are CPU/doc-side and fine in parallel.

SYN speed table line '7S verify + 2(S-1) winner-copy rows (conv+ssm)' conflates: 2(S-1) is the ssm-only term; conv adds ~5-10% of the copy term on top (1.174x -> ~1.18x at S=2, immaterial). Also copy_spec.num_elements semantics (one state column vs whole multi-column block) was read from the call signature (relaunch_qwen36_round.py:811-816) + FR10 design-doc contracts, not the live container mamba_utils source — flagged; a larger copy only worsens multi-spine, so verdict-safe.

SYN speed_verdict 'below the replay-route tree's 0.98-1.11x' mixes units: 0.981x is the replay TIME ratio, 1.02-1.11x is the TPS range; and the SYN omits that the era's actual B=4 SWE s2 campaign ran MTP-3 (12 rows = 1.117x native, per the closeout's mtp=3 arm), normalizing to MTP-5 for E5 comparability — disclosed in reader C's uncertainties but not surfaced in the SYN; neither moves any verdict.
verify.corrected: RE-ATTRIBUTION (grounded, verified in-repo): REFUTED for the measured route. The three cc008587 classes (committer global-RNG, slot-keyed stale accepted-path buffers, in-place shift-left remap race) live in the FR10/FR13 tree stack and did not exist in the multi-spine era. Class-by-class on the FR9 independent-rows arm that produced the binding evidence (era code verified in HEAD scripts/swe_x86_helpers/relaunch_qwen36_round.py): REQKEY absent — keying is req-id based (mamba_state_idx.get(req_id) :778; groups rebuilt per step from input_batch.req_ids :838-841); REMAP race absent — winner copies are batched do_mamba_copy_block memcpys between distinct physical blocks with self-copy skipped (:788, :809-820), and the era LUMO_MULTI_SPINE fork was gather-then-scatter index_select/index_copy_ (0bcfd536); RNG absent — selector OFF (raises, :692-697) and the decisive Gate B probe was greedy; conv prior-window absent — IR mode runs the native conv path (F_b hooks gate on LUMO_FA_UNIQUE_NODES, never set for --row-mode independent). The only era-present cc008587-class hazard is the F_a packed-tree REQKEY machinery (936fecaf: module-global _LUMO_FA_LAST_ACCEPTED_TREE_ROWS :2982/:3322/:3590 with silent linear fallback min(tokens-1, group_size-1) :3415; size-keyed _LUMO_FA_REPLAY_LAYER_SETS :4306) — present but NOT explanatory: FR7's collapse (1.66 vs 3.150) is dominated by the architectural unmasked-shared-scan mechanism, independently confirmed by the 43508c80 contamination measurement (0.5618 vs 2e-5) and by FR13 engineering it out (h_cache+strict_mask, FR13_DECISIVE_TEST.md:5). IMPORTANT QUALIFIER: 'the winner machinery only writes hidden rows' holds for the Era-2 selector-off arm that produced the binding evidence (commit forced to spine-0, :746); Era-1 (65fb6439) DID publish hidden winner rows into spine-0's public stream — that lossy route is what produced +6.85%. The no-go's actual mechanism is distinct and still live: GDN/recurrent-stack batch-composition (+ boot-config) non-invariance, the vLLM #42960 class — the era Gate B arms even booted with different max_num_seqs (4 vs 8, closeout lines 146/173, an uncontrolled confound), and post-cc008587 the greedy B=4 0/4 residual is explicitly 'outside the 3 channels' (FR13_LADDER_LOG.md:1334). So cc008587 predicts no different multi-spine outcome. Evidence quality caveat stands: the no-go was e2e-only, underpowered (1-pair TV floor), judged against a bit-exact-greedy bar native itself fails (native-vs-native 4/8 exact) — overturnable-pending-retest in the narrow evidentiary sense, but not via cc008587, and the user's CLOSED_NON_SHIP binding (968e6bde) additionally rests on non-statistical grounds (copy cost doesn't scale; superset_violations=0 was count-only) untouched by any bug fix. SPEED (recomputed from the actual copy loop): per event the code copies the winner's post-accept state row to all S-1 siblings across 48 GDN layers x BOTH conv+ssm tensors, unconditionally in both modes (:787-821). S=2, B=4, MTP-5: verify 2x7=14 row-touches + ssm copy 1R+1W=2 -> 16 rows x 0.604 GB = 9.66 GB state (+~0.1-0.2 row-equivalents conv); time (27+9.66)/273 = 134.3 ms vs native (27+4.23)/273 = 114.4 ms = 1.174x native (~1.18x with conv); S=3 1.348x, S=4 1.522x. Lossless (selector-off) multi-spine commits spine-0 always -> zero accept gain (measured 3.2364 vs 3.26-3.34) -> 0.85x/0.74x/0.66x native TPS: pure tax, slower than everything. Lossy best-of-spines S=2: tokens/event 4.442/3.772=1.178 cancels the tax -> ~1.00x native on paper at B=4 (consistent with measured low-batch +6.85% and the measured B=4 production loss 0.788x/0.743x with 4/16 vs 8/16 resolved). Vs the replay-route tree (time 0.981x native, TPS 1.02-1.11x with Half-1 fixed; itself counted-touches pending the codegen byte A/B): the second spine's verify alone (4.23 GB) exceeds the entire replay-tree state budget (3.62 GB); break-even needs +19.7%/+37.5%/+55.2% accept at S=2/3/4. That edge is unreachable: at greedy an equal-budget degenerate tree accepts EXACTLY best-of-S (FR13 greedy committer = longest-LCP over any parents array), and at temp>0 the era's own lossy edge measured ~+6-8% tokens/event (5271 recovered tokens / 19,307 events) — well under +19.7%; the lossless tree committer is lossless for any q, and MSS acceptance is monotone in the candidate set, so no lossless variant beats the tree either. Multi-spine additionally pays (S-1) extra full per-sequence KV reads on the 16 full-attn layers (prefix caching dedupes storage, not read bandwidth), growing with context — the table is multi-spine's best case. No crossover at any S on any weight-bandwidth-bound chip; the gap widens with B, context, and recurrent-layer share. Note the era's actual B=4 s2 campaign ran MTP-3 (12 rows = 1.117x native) — smaller tax, same verdict (12 > 6 rows). SUBSUMPTION (verifier AND committer): YES. S spines = a root-fanout-S degenerate tree in the standard candidate-tree descriptor; the FR13 greedy committer (greedy_tree_lcp_max, arbitrary parents array) reduces on that topology to exactly the K-chain best-of-S commit, and the sampled committer is lossless for any q — so the K-chain committer == tree committer on the degenerate tree at greedy, and is dominated by it at temp>0 (lossless vs biased). Physically the tree dominates: one forward over one shared KV with an in-register ancestry bias vs S separate sequences re-reading KV, state cost invariant to candidate count (2+a rows) vs linear in S plus per-event full-state copies. Multi-spine's only legitimate regime is an engine that cannot host a tree verifier (the vLLM-0.19 capture wall that motivated FR9) — an engineering workaround, never a bandwidth winner. RECOMMENDATION (priority corrected): the critical path is the FR13 ACCEPTANCE-DEFICIT LADDER — the open Gate-A verify-forward-drift grind (accept/event 1.199 -> 3.076; FR13_COMMITTER_TOPOLOGY_REDTEAM.md:116-152, FR13_DIRECTION_AND_NUMBERS.md:50/:75, HEAD 2c4da209 'FR13 accept ladder') — per the lossless-first policy; Half-2 replay-route is the separable speed track behind it (WY fallback per the doc). Do NOT pursue a multi-spine retest as a route: (1) the re-attribution fails (distinct, still-live #42960-class mechanism); (2) even a passed powered retest buys nothing — lossless variant 0.85x with zero accept upside by construction, lossy variant user-banned (CLOSED_NON_SHIP 968e6bde, reopening requires explicit user authorization) and only ~1.00x native; (3) no crossover at any S. The ~2-3 GPU-hour native-only max_num_seqs 4-vs-8 cross-boot control is worth running ONLY as ladder-serving noise-floor hygiene (the same #42960 residual gates the FR13 B=4 e2e bar) and must not preempt ladder GPU time; the ~1.5-2 GPU-day powered multi-spine retest is not recommended at any point.
